newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak Sporitelna sees crown holding above parity.
newsitem.headline: Slovak Sporitelna sees crown holding above parity.

text.p: Slovenska Sporitelna a.s., Slovakia's largest savings bank, said on Thursday it expects the crown to hold to the appreciation side of its currency basket midpoint despite a fall in crown deposit rates.

"The interest rate differential players who had boosted trading volumes have left, but the spot traders who do not care about deposit rates have arrived now, and I think we will not fall below parity," Peter Koprna, a Slovenska Sporitelna dealer, said.
By this, Koprna meant that the crown would not move to the depreciation side of the basket midpoint.
The crown is fixed daily by the central bank within a plus/minus 7.0 percent band of its dollar/mark basket midpoint.
The central bank on Thursday fixed the crown at 0.55 percent to the strenthening side of the basket, after fixing it at 0.70 percent stronger on Wednesday.

He said that the crown had neared its parity on Thursday due to a sharp deposit rate fall and another weaker crown fix by the central bank, which had prompted foreign players on the interest rate differential to pull out.
"Until now, the interest rate differential speculators were the trading boosters, which the spot traders are becoming now," he added.
